knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110) with the modular input for `ms:defender:m365`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Defender plans and forward alerts via Microsoft Cloud Services add-on.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="ms:defender:m365" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="ms:defender:m365" severity=High OR severity=Medium
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.98_azure_defender_for_cloud_98"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `ms:defender:m365` in `index=azure` to detect azure defender for cloud high-severity alerts. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_98_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Alert table, severity timeline, resourceId pivot..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure defender for cloud high-severity alerts so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
